title: Examining Korean EFL College Students’ Experiences and Perceptions of Using ChatGPT as a Writing Revision Tool
venue: Journal of English Teaching through Movies and Media
extended_summary:
This study examines how Korean EFL college students experienced and perceived ChatGPT when using it to revise English paragraphs in a general English course focused on academic writing. The paper asks whether students found ChatGPT helpful for revision, what challenges they encountered, and what roles they expected teachers to play when AI tools are used in writing instruction.

The intervention/approach was a classroom-based writing revision activity in which students wrote paragraphs during class and then, as homework, used generative AI chatbots—primarily ChatGPT—to proofread and revise their original texts. Students were not given fixed prompts; instead, they were shown example prompts such as asking the AI to proofread or revise a paragraph. They then completed a survey with Likert-scale and open-ended questions about satisfaction, perceived usefulness, feedback quality, difficulties, and teacher roles. The analysis combined descriptive statistics and thematic analysis.

The participants were 71 Korean university students in a mandatory general English course at a metropolitan four-year university in South Korea. Most were first-year undergraduates and self-identified as English beginners or low-intermediate learners. The findings show generally positive perceptions: students valued ChatGPT’s convenience, immediate feedback, and error correction in vocabulary, grammar, and coherence. However, they also reported problems such as lack of explanations for corrections, overly advanced vocabulary, misaligned responses, uncertainty about learning effectiveness, and a sense that AI revisions sometimes erased their authorship.

Overall, students did not view ChatGPT as a full replacement for teachers. They expected instructors to clarify and verify AI feedback, teach effective prompting, supervise ethical use, and provide emotional encouragement. The paper concludes that ChatGPT can support writing revision as a supplementary tool, but effective integration requires human oversight, guidance on prompt design, and balanced use of AI and teacher feedback.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed qualitative/survey study with descriptive statistics and thematic analysis, but it is not experimental and relies on self-report data from one course cohort. It provides useful implementation evidence, but causal inference is limited.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports positive perceptions and practical benefits, but no objective learning gains or effect sizes were measured. The impact is therefore suggestive and modest/unclear rather than demonstrated at scale.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT used as a writing revision chatbot for Korean EFL college students to proofread and revise paragraphs, generate feedback on grammar, vocabulary, clarity, coherence, and organization, and provide alternative rewritten versions.
Generative AI writing support for EFL paragraph revision, including proofreading, vocabulary replacement, coherence editing, and content enrichment in academic writing assignments.

finding.finding_summary: Students reported generally positive experiences using ChatGPT for paragraph revision in a general English academic writing course (n=71). Satisfaction with receiving feedback and revising with ChatGPT was high (M=4.13/5, SD=0.79), and students rated its help for vocabulary, grammar, clarity, coherence, and organization positively (e.g., vocabulary/expression M=4.23, grammar M=4.17).
finding.measure: Student survey ratings of satisfaction, helpfulness, and perceived improvement in writing quality; thematic responses about revision benefits

finding.finding_summary: Students expressed strong willingness to continue using ChatGPT for future paragraph editing (M=4.21/5, SD=0.91) and described the tool as convenient, fast, and reassuring. Qualitative comments also noted increased confidence and satisfaction, though some students worried about frustration, anxiety, and diminished authorship.
finding.measure: Future-use intention, satisfaction, and thematic comments on convenience/confidence

finding.finding_summary: The study suggests some metacognitive support from ChatGPT because students used it to identify errors and compare revisions, but many also reported uncertainty about learning effectiveness and difficulty critically evaluating AI feedback. The authors highlight that students often needed teacher guidance to interpret outputs, which limits claims of independent skill development.
finding.measure: Survey responses and open-ended reflections on understanding feedback and evaluating revisions

finding.finding_summary: Students strongly valued the time-saving and always-available nature of ChatGPT for revision, describing it as easy, fast, and hassle-free. Qualitative responses emphasized instant replies and no restrictions of time or place, indicating improved efficiency in obtaining writing feedback.
finding.measure: Survey Likert items and thematic comments on convenience, instant reply, and access

finding.finding_summary: Students did not believe generative AI could fully replace human instructors for feedback (M=2.35/5, SD=1.10), and most preferred either a combination of ChatGPT and instructors or instructors only. They expected teachers to clarify AI feedback, verify accuracy, teach prompt use and ethical practices, and provide emotional support, implying a blended human-AI instructional model rather than replacement.
finding.measure: Survey item on replacement of instructor feedback; choice between ChatGPT and instructor feedback; thematic analysis of anticipated teacher roles
